summary: No further evidence can be produced before expiry, so this points at the retained draft as it stands; the run ended with all necessary gaps closed and no open questions in the controller's list. Final state of the audit: the snapshot is unmodified upstream etcd-raft v3.7.0 at commit b867cf13, and six threads are recorded. Two sourced defects are asserted with retained executions. First, read-index retry growth: ReadOnlySafe admission is per request and context-blind, so same-context retries accumulate one queued or unconfirmed entry each, with no library-side bound and no reclamation while the process lives, and the accumulated queue is released later as a burst of one admission plus one heartbeat per entry; receipts cover the queued path and its retention across deposition, the admitted path, the release burst, a CheckQuorum control that closes the growth window at step-down while retaining the state, a byte measurement of caller payload (262144 bytes for 64 requests with 4 KiB contexts in 64 distinct buffers), and a real isolated-leader network run where 32 requests produced confirmed zero and 64 heartbeats, correcting the amplification to one heartbeat per peer per retry. Second, configuration change: in a joint configuration with no change pending unapplied, an empty ConfChangeV2 whose transition is not Auto passes propose-time validation as an EntryConfChangeV2, commits in a real three-node network, and panics the application in ApplyConfChange with config is already joint, because validation derives leave-joint from an empty change set while the apply path also requires the Auto transition, with the Auto form as the working control and the pending-conf guard as a precondition. The four remaining threads are explained or refuted with their boundaries stated: readOnly ack validation out of contract, queued read requests kept fresh across term changes by the monotonic commit index, the StateSnapshot repair duty with both exits measured, and proposer eligibility of removed members belonging to the caller under the documented MsgProp contract.
